# Paid Live Mission 4 — Project Brain v2, the trust core.
#
# THE DELIVERABLE. A real Sunday Relay file, sliced byte-identical, so the diff
# this mission produces applies straight back to the repository.
src/relay/mission/julius/julius-memory-trust.ts

# WHAT IT IS TYPED AGAINST. `julius-memory-trust.ts` imports only a TYPE from
# here, which type stripping erases — so nothing loads this file at runtime
# today. It is sliced anyway for two reasons: the coder has to READ the role
# union it is writing against, and the day anyone turns that into a value
# import the module must already be present rather than failing inside a paid
# run. Its own import of `julius-repair-lineage` is why that file is here too:
# a slice whose import chain stops halfway is a sandbox that works until it
# doesn't.
src/relay/mission/julius/julius-runtime.ts
src/relay/mission/julius/julius-repair-lineage.ts
src/relay/mission/julius/julius-segment-lineage.ts

# AND THE TWO FILES THE CHAIN GREW AFTER THIS LIST WAS WRITTEN. The comment
# above got the rule right and the list stopped following it: `julius-runtime`
# now imports the context integrity layer as a VALUE, and
# `julius-repair-lineage` imports `julius-segment-lineage` as one. Both hops
# were missing from every slice manifest here, so provisioning this mission and
# running its own declared test command died on ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND before an
# assertion ran. `scripts/julius-mission-slice.test.ts` now resolves every
# relative import of every slice mission transitively, so the next hop that
# grows fails `npm test` rather than a paid run.
src/relay/mission/julius/julius-context-integrity.ts
